extracted.intended_audience: ORR staff, ORR care provider facilities, child welfare practitioners, legal advocates, and policymakers involved in care/placement of unaccompanied children
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulatory standards for Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) care, placement, emergency/influx facility operations, review procedures (restrictive placement, PRP, risk hearings), and the Unaccompanied Children Office of the Ombuds duties and requirements. Includes minimum services, placement criteria, review timelines, and Ombuds authorities and confidentiality rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age-assessment ambiguity rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambiguous, debatable, or borderline forensic examination results are resolved in favor of finding the individual is a minor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold applies to all medical methods and approaches identified by the medical community as appropriate methods for assessing age.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of an individual who appears to be an adult
rubrics_metrics.description: If procedures would result in a reasonable person concluding that an individual is an adult, despite the individual's claim to be under the age of 18, ORR shall treat such person as an adult for all purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency planning and reevaluation of placements
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR regularly reevaluates the number of placements needed for unaccompanied children and implements contingency planning and procedures during an emergency or influx.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In an emergency/influx ORR will make reasonable efforts to place each child in a standard program expeditiously; activities include implementing contingency plans (which may include opening facilities and prioritizing placement), developing standard programs for emergency placements, and maintaining a list of affected unaccompanied children with name, date and country of birth, date of placement in ORR custody, and place and date of current placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency/influx facilities must provide proper physical care and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide suitable living accommodations, food, appropriate clothing, and personal grooming items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency/influx facilities must provide appropriate routine medical and dental care
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide routine medical and dental care, family planning services (including pregnancy tests), medical services requiring heightened ORR involvement, emergency healthcare services, and a complete medical examination (including infectious disease screenings) within 48 hours of admission (excluding weekends/holidays) unless recently examined at another ORR facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide appropriate immunizations as recommended by ACIP/CDC, administration of prescribed medication and special diets, and appropriate mental health interventions when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency/influx facilities must perform an individualized needs assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: An individualized needs assessment must include initial intake forms, collection of essential identifying and family history data, identification of special needs requiring immediate intervention, an educational assessment and plan, assessment of family relationships and interaction with adults/peers/authority figures, statement of religious preference and practice, assessment of personal goals/strengths/weaknesses, and identifying information regarding immediate family/relatives/godparents/friends in the U.S. who may assist in connecting the child with family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency/influx facilities must provide educational services appropriate to level and communication skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational services in a structured classroom setting Monday through Friday focusing primarily on basic academic competencies and secondarily on English language acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program shall include instruction and reading materials in necessary languages; basic academic areas should include science, social studies, math, reading, writing, and physical education; provide reading materials in languages other than English for leisure time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recreation and leisure time plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities according to a recreation and leisure time plan that include daily outdoor activity—weather permitting—with at least one hour per day of large muscle activity and one hour per day of structured leisure time activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should not include time watching television; on days when school is not in session, activities should be increased to a total of three hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual counseling frequency and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one individual counseling session per week conducted by trained social work staff to review the child's progress, establish new short-term objectives, and address developmental and crisis-related needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group counseling frequency and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Group counseling sessions at least twice a week; usually informal and take place with all unaccompanied children present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sessions allow new children to get acquainted with staff/other children and program rules, provide an open forum for discussion, daily program management, and problem resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acculturation and adaptation services
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information and services regarding development of social and interpersonal skills necessary to live independently and responsibly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive orientation on program rules and legal assistance availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a comprehensive orientation regarding program intent, services, rules (written and verbal), expectations, and availability of legal assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to religious services
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever possible, provide access to religious services of the child's choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visitation and contact with family members
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide visitation and contact with family members (regardless of immigration status), structured to encourage visitation while respecting the child's privacy and reasonably preventing unauthorized release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable right to privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the right to wear own clothes when available, retain private storage space, talk privately on the phone and visit privately with guests as permitted by house rules, and receive and send uncensored mail unless there is reasonable belief it contains contraband.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services to identify relatives and assistance obtaining legal guardianship
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide services designed to identify relatives in the United States and foreign countries and assist in obtaining legal guardianship when necessary for release of the unaccompanied child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal services information and rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform children about availability of free legal assistance, right to be represented by counsel at no expense to the government, right to a removal hearing before an immigration judge, ability to apply for asylum with USCIS, and ability to request voluntary departure in lieu of deportation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with State child welfare and building/safety codes to greatest extent possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency/influx facilities, whether state-licensed or not, must comply to the greatest extent possible with State child welfare laws/regulations and applicable State/local building, fire, health, and safety codes; ORR will review potential conflicts between ORR regulations and State law to ensure statutory responsibilities are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If State law or license conflicts with an ORR employee's duties within the scope of ORR employment, the ORR employee is required to abide by their Federal duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver services sensitive to age, culture, native language, and needs; individual service plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency or influx facilities must deliver services in a manner sensitive to each child's age, culture, native language, and needs, and must develop an individual service plan for each child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and confidentiality/accountability systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency or influx facilities must maintain records of case files, make regular reports to ORR, and have accountability systems that preserve confidentiality and protect records from unauthorized use or disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain safe and sanitary conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency or influx facilities must maintain safe and sanitary conditions consistent with ORR's concern for the particular vulnerability of minors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide access to toilets, showers, sinks, and hygiene items
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide access to toilets, showers and sinks, and personal hygiene items such as soap, toothpaste/toothbrush, floss, towels, feminine care items, and similar items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide drinking water and food
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency or influx facilities must provide drinking water and food.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide emergency medical assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide medical assistance if the unaccompanied child is in need of emergency services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain adequate temperature control and ventilation
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency or influx facilities must maintain adequate temperature control and ventilation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide adequate supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide adequate supervision to protect unaccompanied children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate children who pose a danger to self/others
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate from other unaccompanied children those children subsequently found to have past criminal or juvenile detention histories or who have perpetrated sexual abuse that present a danger to themselves or others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide contact with family members arrested with the child
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contact with family members who were arrested with the unaccompanied child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide access to legal services per §410.701(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide access to the legal services described in §410.701(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waivers for emergency/influx facility standards
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may grant waivers from standards under paragraph (b) if the facility is activated for six consecutive months or less and the standards are operationally infeasible, provided waivers are done in accordance with law and made publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement eligibility: expected release within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Unaccompanied children placed in emergency/influx facilities should be expected to be released to a sponsor within 30 days, to the extent feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a child later is found not to meet criteria, ORR will transfer the child to the least restrictive appropriate setting expeditiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement eligibility: minimum age
rubrics_metrics.description: Unaccompanied child should be age 13 or older to the extent feasible for emergency/influx placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement eligibility: preferred language
rubrics_metrics.description: Unaccompanied child should speak English or Spanish as their preferred language to the extent feasible for emergency/influx placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement eligibility: no known disability/medical/dental issue requiring extra care
rubrics_metrics.description: Child should not have a known disability or other mental health, medical, or dental issue requiring additional evaluation, treatment, or monitoring by a healthcare provider to the extent feasible for emergency/influx placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement eligibility: not pregnant or parenting teen
rubrics_metrics.description: Child should not be a pregnant or parenting teen to the extent feasible for emergency/influx placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement eligibility: no diminution of legal services
rubrics_metrics.description: Placement in an unlicensed facility should not result in a diminution of legal services for the child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement eligibility: not a danger to self or others
rubrics_metrics.description: Child should not be a danger to self or others (including not having been charged with or convicted of a criminal offense) to the extent feasible for emergency/influx placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement considerations: sibling grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR should avoid placing a child in an emergency/influx facility if the child is part of a sibling group with sibling(s) age 12 years or younger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement considerations: pending age determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Child should not be subject to a pending age determination when placed in an emergency/influx facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement considerations: active investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Child should not be involved in an active State licensing, child protective services, law enforcement investigation, or an investigation from a sexual abuse allegation when placed in an emergency/influx facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement considerations: pending home study
rubrics_metrics.description: Child should not have a pending home study when placed in an emergency/influx facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement considerations: near 18th birthday
rubrics_metrics.description: Child should not be turning 18 years old within 30 days of transfer to an emergency/influx facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement considerations: imminent discharge
rubrics_metrics.description: Child should not be scheduled to be discharged in three days or less when transferred to an emergency/influx facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement considerations: immigration/court status and counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Child should not have a current set docket date in immigration or state/family court, not have a pending adjustment of legal status, and not have an attorney of record or EOIR-accredited representative when placed in an emergency/influx facility, to the extent feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement considerations: medical clearance and vaccination
rubrics_metrics.description: Child should be medically cleared and vaccinated as required by the emergency/influx care facility (e.g., DOD site requirements) when placed in such facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement considerations: no known contagious or health issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Child should have no known mental health, dental, or medical issues, including contagious diseases requiring additional evaluation, treatment, or monitoring by a healthcare provider, when placed in an emergency/influx facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictive placement standard of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: For placement in a restrictive setting, ORR shall determine, based on clear and convincing evidence, that sufficient grounds exist for stepping up or continuing to hold an unaccompanied child in a restrictive placement; supporting evidence shall be recorded in the child's case file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Placement (NOP) timing and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall provide an unaccompanied child with a Notice of Placement no later than 48 hours after step-up to a restrictive placement, and every 30 days the child remains in restrictive placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOP must be timely and repeated every 30 days while in restrictive placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Placement (NOP) contents and explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: The NOP shall clearly and thoroughly set forth the reason(s) for placement and a summary of supporting evidence; inform the child of their right to contest the placement before a Placement Review Panel (PRP) and the procedures to do so; inform of all available administrative review processes; and include an explanation of the child's right to be represented by counsel in challenging the placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A case manager must explain the NOP to the child in a language the child understands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of NOP copies
rubrics_metrics.description: The care provider facility shall provide a copy of the NOP to the child's legal counsel of record, legal service provider, child advocate, and a parent or legal guardian of record no later than 48 hours after step-up and every 30 days the child remains in restrictive placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic administrative review schedule for restrictive placements
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall ensure automatic administrative reviews: at minimum a 30-day administrative review for all restrictive placements; a more intensive 45-day review by ORR supervisory staff for children in secure facilities; and for children in RTCs the 30-day review must involve a psychiatrist or psychologist to determine whether the child should remain in restrictive residential care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement Review Panel (PRP) hearing rights and process
rubrics_metrics.description: A child placed in a restrictive placement may request reconsideration and shall be afforded a hearing before the PRP where the child may, with counsel if preferred, present evidence, present witnesses, and cross-examine ORR's witnesses if willing to testify; the child may alternatively submit a request for reconsideration with supporting documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PRP must afford review as soon as the child receives the NOP, convene without undue delay, and issue a decision within 30 calendar days of the PRP request whenever possible; an ORR staff member involved in the step-up decision may not serve as a PRP member for that child's placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk determination hearings for restrictive placements
rubrics_metrics.description: All children in restrictive placements shall be afforded a hearing before an independent HHS hearing officer to determine, by written decision, whether the child would present a danger to the community unless the child refuses in writing; other children in ORR custody may request such a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be written (child, attorney, or parent/guardian); children placed in restrictive placements based on dangerousness receive an automatic hearing unless they refuse in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof in risk determination hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: In risk determination hearings, ORR bears the initial burden of production to support its determination that the child would pose a danger if discharged; the burden of persuasion is on the child to show they will not be a danger to the community if released, using a preponderance of the evidence standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk hearing procedures and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: In hearings under this section, the child may be represented by a person of their choosing, present oral and written evidence, and may appear by video or teleconference; ORR may also present evidence in writing or appear in person or by video/teleconference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding nature of hearing officer decision and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: A hearing officer's decision that a child would not be a danger if released is binding on ORR unless appealed; decisions under this section may be appealed by either the child or ORR to the Assistant Secretary of ACF within 30 days of the hearing officer decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Assistant Secretary reviews the record and will reverse only for a clear error of fact or an error of law. If a hearing officer finds the child not dangerous and release would follow, an appeal to the Assistant Secretary shall not stay the release unless the Assistant Secretary issues a written stay within five business days including a description of behaviors and/or documented criminal/juvenile records demonstrating danger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality and rehearing standards for risk determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions under this section are final and binding on the Department; a child determined to pose a danger may only seek another hearing by demonstrating a material change in circumstances; ORR may request a new determination if at least one month has passed since the original decision and/or ORR can show a material change in circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section cannot be used to determine whether a child has a suitable sponsor, nor may it be invoked to determine the child's placement or level of custody while in ORR custody.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and independence of UC Office of the Ombuds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Unaccompanied Children Office of the Ombuds (UC Office of the Ombuds) is located within the Office of the ACF Assistant Secretary and shall be an independent, impartial office with authority to receive reports (including confidential/informal), investigate concerns regarding care of unaccompanied children, work collaboratively with ORR to resolve reports, and issue reports concerning its efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: UC Ombuds policies, transparency, and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: The UC Office of the Ombuds shall develop appropriate standards, practices, policies and procedures (considering nationally recognized ombudsperson recommendations), make standards/practices/reports/findings/policies publicly available, and make information about the office and how to contact it publicly available in English and other languages spoken and understood by unaccompanied children in ORR care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ombuds may identify preferred methods for raising awareness such as visiting ORR facilities or publishing aggregated information about concerns and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: UC Ombuds scope of activities and authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The UC Office of the Ombuds may engage in activities including receiving reports from children, potential sponsors and stakeholders; investigating ORR adherence to law/regulations; requesting and receiving relevant information/documents from ORR and care providers; preparing formal reports/recommendations including an annual report; conducting investigations/interviews/site visits; visiting care providers; reviewing individual circumstances (access to services, communication, transfers, discharge matters); making efforts to resolve complaints; hiring/retaining experts, specialists, interpreters; making non-binding recommendations to ORR; providing general educational information about laws/regulations/advocacy/legal services; and advising/updating ORR leadership on implementation and adherence to law/policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: UC Ombuds referral authority and access needs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ombuds may refer matters to other Federal agencies or offices with jurisdiction (including Federal/State law enforcement) and shall have timely/direct access to unaccompanied children in ORR care, ORR care provider facilities, case file information, care provider and Federal staff responsible for children's care, and statistical/other ORR data as needed to accomplish its work.

rubrics_metrics.name: UC Ombuds staffing, qualifications, and training
rubrics_metrics.description: The UC Ombuds shall be hired as a career civil servant and should have requisite knowledge and experience (including membership in a nationally recognized ombuds/association or State bar) and demonstrated knowledge/experience in informal dispute resolution, services related to unaccompanied children and child welfare, oversight and regulatory matters, and ORR policy and regulations; the Ombuds may engage additional staff and shall establish procedures for training, certification, and continuing education for staff and representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: UC Ombuds confidentiality and non-use for immigration enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ombuds shall manage files/records/information in a manner that preserves confidentiality except in instances of imminent harm or judicial action and is prohibited from using or sharing information for any immigration enforcement-related purpose; the Ombuds may accept anonymous reports of concerns.
